title: candidate.measured
description: A program was built into a circuit and scored by the verifier. This is the only event that carries a result. Failures are recorded here too (passes=false) rather than discarded — a failure plus its reason is the most useful signal a lab assistant can be given. SUBJECT IS prog:<the program measured>, not a separate candidate id: a candidate is not an independent entity with its own lifecycle, it is one (program, config) run. Keeping the program as subject means history('prog:...') returns the commit AND every measurement of it, which is the query you actually want. Several candidates from one program under different configs therefore share a subject.

program.description: Digest of the program that produced this candidate. Join key to program.committed, and through its `cause` field, to the direction that prompted it.

cost.description: The competition cost. LOWER IS BETTER. Always present, always a single scalar — this is what makes frontier() work identically across benchmarks and across every future loop generation. For invsqrt: Q x (Toffolis + T/4). COMPARABLE ONLY WITHIN THE SAME `verifier` VALUE; a verifier upgrade can shift costs, so never compare across versions without checking.

passes.description: True only if the verifier accepted EVERY shot. A single bad shot means false. frontier() considers only passing candidates, but failing ones stay in the log deliberately.

benchmark.description: Which competition task, e.g. 'invsqrt'. Denormalized from the program for query convenience.

metrics.description: Benchmark-specific numbers. Free-form by design, so dqi can add eps_plus and dfthcsos can add lambda_eff with no schema change. For invsqrt use {"Q": <qubits>, "T": <toffoli_equivalents>}. Baseline for reference: Q=260, T=7735, cost=2011100.

circuit.description: Digest of the serialized circuit (.kmb/.kmx), blob kind 'circuit', or null if not retained. SAFE TO GARBAGE COLLECT: (program, config) regenerates it deterministically, so dropping one costs seconds rather than information.

config.description: The parameters the program was run with. Recorded so the circuit can be regenerated after GC, and so parameter sweeps are analysable. Keep small — event lines must stay under 4 KB for atomic append; spill to a blob if large.

rung.description: Which verification tier produced this: conventionally 'smoke' (~1e3 shots), 'screen' (~1e5), or 'full' (~2e8 x 4 seeds). Advisory only — the ladder will change. Judge trustworthiness from `shots` and `seeds`, not from this label.

shots.description: Total shots simulated. Free, but record it consistently: a free field written by convention can be promoted to frozen later and will then work retroactively over all history.

seeds.description: Verifier seeds used. NEVER TRUST A SINGLE SEED. The leaderboard seeds its tests from the circuit's SHA-256 combined with a secret salt, and any edit to a circuit draws a fresh test set, so a candidate passing on one seed may be lucky rather than correct. Nothing should be submitted on fewer than four independent seeds.

verifier.description: Verifier identity and version, e.g. 'kickmix@1.2.0'. Essential: kickmix is migrating to PyPI during this competition, and after an upgrade you must be able to tell which half of your history is still comparable.

cost_basis.description: SEMANTIC TAG: what `cost` actually means, independent of what the field is called. e.g. 'invsqrt/QxC/v1' for Q x (Toffolis + T/4). This is the defence against the worst schema failure — a field keeping its name while its meaning drifts. Two values are comparable only if their cost_basis matches; a consumer that sees two different bases knows it must not compare them, rather than silently producing a confident wrong answer.

failure.description: Present when passes=false. Conventionally {class, first_failing_input, detail}. Free-form — the useful failure taxonomy is not knowable in advance.

x-accessors._comment: Which accessor in substrate/accessors.py reads which field IN THIS VERSION. This is the real dependency graph: to change a field, add a branch to the named accessor and a conformance fixture for this version. Nothing else in the system names these fields.
